lessons.title: Getting ready to harvest fish
lessons.html:
What is harvesting?

Harvesting means taking fish out of the pond or tank. Some fish go to market. Some go to another tank. Fish are alive and can get hurt or stressed. Stressed fish get sick and the meat is poorer. So we harvest with care.

Before harvest day

  • Your supervisor tells you which pond or tank and how many fish.
  • Stop feeding the fish for the time the supervisor says, often one day before. Fish with empty guts handle stress better and stay cleaner.
  • Check that all equipment is ready and clean.
  • Check that there is clean water and ice if fish go to market.

Equipment you will use

  • Seine nets to pull through a pond.
  • Scoop nets with soft mesh.
  • Baskets, crates or bins.
  • Tanks with clean water and air for live fish.
  • Scales to weigh fish.
  • Ice and cooler boxes for fish that go to market.

Look for holes in nets. Fish escape through holes. Wash and disinfect nets and crates between ponds. This stops disease moving from one pond to another.

Best time to harvest

Harvest early in the morning when water is cool. Fish are calmer. Hot water holds less oxygen, so fish get stressed fast in the heat. Avoid harvesting in the hottest part of the day.

Safety for you

  • Wear gumboots or waders with good grip. Pond edges are slippery.
  • Never work alone in deep water. Always have a partner.
  • Watch for electric cables and pumps near water. Switch off pumps before working in the water if your supervisor says so.
  • Wear gloves. Catfish and tilapia have sharp spines.

If you cannot swim, do not go into deep water. Tell your supervisor.

lessons.title: Handling fish gently
lessons.html:
Keep fish calm and wet

Fish breathe through their gills. Gills only work in water. A fish out of water cannot breathe. Keep fish out of the water for as short a time as you can.

Good handling

  1. Crowd the fish slowly with the net. Do not chase them.
  2. Scoop small numbers at a time. Too many fish in one net crush each other.
  3. Use wet hands or wet gloves. Dry hands remove the slime that protects the fish.
  4. Hold a fish gently under the belly. Do not squeeze it.
  5. Never throw or drop fish.
  6. Put fish straight into clean water with air, or onto ice if they go to market.

Signs of stress

  • Fish gasping at the surface.
  • Fish swimming on their side.
  • Lost scales and red marks.

If you see these signs, slow down and tell your supervisor. Add air to the water if you can.

Fish for the market

Fish for food must stay cold and clean. Put them on clean ice in cooler boxes. Keep them out of the sun. Keep the area, the crates and your hands clean. Fish spoil fast when warm. Dirty fish can make people sick.

Weigh and write down

Count and weigh the fish. Write the pond number, the number of fish, the total mass and the date. The farm needs this to know how well the fish grew and how much to pay or charge.

After the harvest

  • Wash and disinfect nets, crates and boots.
  • Pack away equipment dry.
  • Report any dead or sick fish.

Key points

  • Stop feeding before harvest as your supervisor says.
  • Harvest in the cool morning.
  • Keep fish out of water for as short a time as you can.
  • Use wet hands and never throw fish.
  • Keep market fish cold, clean and on ice.
